# A one-sided entropy upper bound for stable matchings

Local research draft, 2026-09-21; formalization status updated 2026-09-22.
The original conclusion f(n)<3.332^n has a complete Lean proof.
A [later numerical refinement](entropy-improvement-limits.md) establishes
f(n)<3.331974^n through the same finite permutation argument and a sharper
checked enclosure. The [current theorem guide](entropy-lean-proof.md)
now describes the complete 3.2 Lean theorem, which adds structural
constraints and uses both directions.
The stronger infinite-series expression exp(Cn) in this draft remains a
written derivation. Independent mathematical review and priority remain
open. Nothing has been pushed or submitted. See the
[plan and reflection log](entropy-formalization-plan.md).

## Statement

Let S(I) be the stable matchings of a complete strict marriage instance
with n men and n women. Put

\[
 C=\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{2\log k}{(k+1)(k+2)}.
\]

The argument below gives, for every n >= 1,

\[
 |S(I)|\leq \exp(Cn)<(3.332)^n,
 \qquad f(n)\leq \exp(Cn)<(3.332)^n.                 \tag{1}
\]

All logarithms are natural. The proof applies to arbitrary rotation sizes
and uses neither a restriction on schedules nor an asymptotic independence
approximation. The numerical certificate proves

\[
 C<1.203565300089<\log(833/250).
\]

The proposed improvement is the one-sided encoding together with the
stable-pair separation argument. The series C is already present in
Section 3.4, equation (3), of
[Palmer and Palvolgyi](https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.00915), where a different
encoding incurs twice this exponent for tangled grids. This draft does
not claim a better bound for arbitrary tangled grids.

## 1. A stable pair separates the other stable partners

Write x >_v y when participant v strictly prefers x to y. A pair (m,w)
is a stable pair if it belongs to at least one member of S(I).

**Lemma 1.** Let (m,w) be a stable pair, and let mu be any stable
matching with mu(m) != w. Then

\[
 w>_m\mu(m)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \mu^{-1}(w)>_w m.                                \tag{2}
\]

**Proof.** Choose a stable matching nu containing (m,w). On a nontrivial
alternating cycle of mu and nu, write

\[
 \mu(m_i)=w_i,\qquad \nu(m_i)=w_{i+1},
\]

with cyclic subscripts. If m_i prefers w_i to w_{i+1}, stability of nu
forces w_i to prefer m_{i-1} to m_i. Stability of mu then forces m_{i-1}
to prefer w_{i-1} to w_i. Repeating around the cycle shows that every man
on it prefers mu and every woman on it prefers nu. If no man on the cycle
prefers mu, strictness makes all of them prefer nu; stability of mu then
makes all women prefer mu. Thus on each differing edge of nu its two
endpoints have opposite preferences between mu and nu. Apply this to
(m,w). QED.

This is the classical decomposition/opposition property, not a new
lemma. See Roth, Rothblum and Vande Vate (1993), Lemma 11, p. 811,
in their [author PDF](https://web.stanford.edu/~alroth/papers/1993_MOR_StableMatchingsOptimal.pdf),
which credits Knuth (1976). The proof is included to avoid dependence on
a rotation-poset representation. The [literature audit](entropy-literature-audit-2026-09-21.md)
separates these known ingredients from the candidate combination.

**Consequence.** List the stable partners of a fixed man m in his
preference order as w_0,...,w_(d-1). If a woman w_j in this list has a
fixed partner u != m, then all stable matchings consistent with this
fixed pair put m strictly on the same side of position j. The side is
determined by whether w_j prefers u to m, by (2). These fixed women
therefore act as ordered barriers, not merely as unavailable partners.

## 2. Revealing men also fixes their partners' inverse coordinates

Choose a stable matching M uniformly from S(I). Independently give each
man u a uniform priority U_u in (0,1), and reveal the coordinates M(u)
in increasing priority order. The revelation order is independent of M.

For a fixed outcome mu, define

\[
 R_m=\{u:U_u<U_m\},\qquad
 X_m(\mu,U)=|\{\nu(m):\nu\in S(I),\quad
                 \nu(u)=\mu(u)\text{ for all }u\in R_m\}|.
\]

This is the exact conditional support size before revealing m. For each
fixed revelation order, the entropy chain rule and the support bound on
each conditional entropy give

\[
 \log|S(I)|=H(M)
 \leq\sum_m\mathbb E_{M,U}\log X_m(M,U).           \tag{3}
\]

Here the support bound is applied separately to each complete revealed
prefix. It does not condition only on the numerical size of the support.
The counting inequality is also Lemma 4 of Palmer and Palvolgyi; it is
not claimed as a new entropy theorem.

Fix mu and m, and write mu(m)=w_t in m's ordered stable-partner list.
Revealing any u != m fixes both mu(u) and its inverse partner u. Let

\[
 a=\max(\{-1\}\cup\{j<t:\mu^{-1}(w_j)\in R_m\}),
 \qquad
 b=\min(\{d\}\cup\{j>t:\mu^{-1}(w_j)\in R_m\}).
\]

The endpoint values -1 and d are fixed sentinels. Lemma 1 gives the
pointwise support inclusion

\[
 \{\nu(m):\nu|_{R_m}=\mu|_{R_m},\ \nu\in S(I)\}
 \subseteq\{w_{a+1},...,w_{b-1}\}.
\]

In particular,

\[
 X_m(\mu,U)\leq b-a-1.                            \tag{4}
\]

The interval need not be filled: all unmodeled stability constraints can
only remove choices. No converse to the inclusion is used.

## 3. Exact independence and the gap distribution

Condition on U_m=x, with 0 < x < 1. For fixed mu, the men

\[
 \mu^{-1}(w_j),\qquad j\ne t,
\]

are distinct and all differ from m. Their priorities are independent.
Consequently each barrier position j != t is revealed independently
with probability x. The left and right barrier sets are also independent.

This is an exact finite-n statement. The proof samples a fixed order of
men independently of the matching; it does not choose a matching-dependent
order of couples. The matching-dependent inverse map is used only to
analyze that fixed random order, after mu has been fixed.

Let L=t-a and R=b-t. Pad each side of the finite list with further
independent Bernoulli(x) trials. Under this coupling,

\[
 L=\min(G_1,t+1),\qquad R=\min(G_2,d-t),
\]

where G_1,G_2 are independent geometric(x) variables supported on
1,2,... . Thus, pointwise under the coupling,

\[
 X_m\leq L+R-1\leq G_1+G_2-1=:K_x.
\]

There are k positive ordered pairs with sum k+1, so

\[
 \Pr(K_x=k)=k x^2(1-x)^{k-1},\qquad k\geq1.        \tag{5}
\]

The values x=0 and x=1 need no special limit argument in the expectation:
they have measure zero. Integrating over the uniform priority of m and
using nonnegativity to interchange sum and integral gives, for every
fixed mu and m,

\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_U\log X_m(\mu,U)
 &\leq\int_0^1\sum_{k\geq1}k x^2(1-x)^{k-1}\log k\,dx\\
 &=\sum_{k\geq1}\frac{2\log k}{(k+1)(k+2)}=C.
 \end{aligned}                                    \tag{6}
\]

The beta integral is elementary, and the series converges by comparison
with 2 log(k)/k^2. Averaging (6) over mu and substituting into (3) proves
the first inequality in (1). The argument includes empty sides of the
partner list and the unique-matching case d=1.

## 4. A rigorous numerical bound

[entropy_upper_bound.py](../tools/entropy_upper_bound.py) uses integer
arithmetic throughout its certificate. For y in [1,2], put
z=(y-1)/(y+1). The identity

\[
 \log y=2\sum_{i=0}^{q-1}\frac{z^{2i+1}}{2i+1}+E_q,
 \qquad 0\leq E_q\leq
 \frac{2z^{2q+1}}{(2q+1)(1-z^2)}
\]

provides rational enclosures after range reduction by powers of two.
Each summand is rounded outward on an integer grid with denominator
10^24; 32 terms suffice for the logarithms used here.

For the remaining positive series after N=10000,

\[
 \sum_{k>N}\frac{2\log k}{(k+1)(k+2)}
 \leq\sum_{k>N}\frac{2\log k}{k^2}
 \leq\int_N^\infty\frac{2\log x}{x^2}\,dx
 =\frac{2(\log N+1)}{N}.
\]

The final comparison, with common denominator 10^24, is

```text
C upper:          1203565300088168472557988 / 10^24
log(3.332) lower:  1203572724304596257240710 / 10^24
strict margin:          7424216427784682722 / 10^24
```

This proves the strict second inequality in (1). The value 3.332 is a
convenient rational upper bound, not a claimed exact growth constant.

## 5. Finite checks and their limits

[validate_entropy_bound.py](../tools/validate_entropy_bound.py) builds
stable matchings directly from blocking constraints. It checks (2) for
every stable pair against every enumerated stable matching. It also
intersects exact matching fibers after revealing men, and checks the
full support inclusion (4), not only its cardinality. Matching sets
through order nine are independently compared with permutation search.

The validation covers every order-three profile, stable matching, man,
and reveal subset; seeded larger instances; and retained extremal
witnesses. The capped geometric model is independently compared, using
exact fractions, with all reveal subsets for 49 choices of side lengths.
Tests also compare the integer logarithm enclosures with independent
high-precision Decimal logarithms.

Whenever all reveal subsets and stable outcomes are checked, a further
end-to-end diagnostic verifies that log|S(I)| is bounded by the averaged
logarithm of the exact support, then by the averaged logarithm of the
barrier interval. The latter is independently reconstructed from the
capped geometric distribution. This diagnostic uses floating arithmetic;
the certificate for the constant uses only integers.

These computations guard against concrete mistakes. The all-order claim
comes from Sections 1-4, not extrapolation from the tested instances.
The retained [evidence and exact counts](../results/entropy-upper-bound-2026-09-21/README.md)
record the completed checks and source identities.

## 6. Baseline reproduction issue

The first audit attempted to reproduce the displayed final constant in
Claim 24 of the [arXiv version](https://arxiv.org/html/2011.00915v2) and
the [FOCS proceedings version](https://ieee-focs.org/FOCS-2021-Papers/pdfs/FOCS2021-5stbVHiOp5jRHWlSl41FkR/205500a217/205500a217.pdf)
of Palmer and Palvolgyi. Both display

\[
 \frac{\log2}{12}+\frac{23\log3}{630}
 +\sum_{k\geq4}(\log k)
   \frac{2k(k+7)+72}{(k+3)(k+5)(k+6)(k+7)}
 \leq0.6331.
\]

The displayed series, read literally, does not satisfy that numerical
inequality: its positive partial sum through k=10000 already exceeds
0.691931726947. Exact integration of the displayed probabilities gives
the displayed coefficients again. The certificate records this mismatch
separately. It identifies a problem in this specific displayed calculation;
it does not establish that the paper's main theorem is false or exclude
a repair. No authors have been contacted. The proof in Sections 1-4 does
not use Claim 24 or the disputed numerical calculation.

## Reproduction and remaining review

Use fresh output paths; the tools refuse to overwrite evidence:

```bash
python3 tools/entropy_upper_bound.py --output runs/entropy-constant-review.json
python3 tools/validate_entropy_bound.py --output runs/entropy-validation-review.json
python3 -m unittest tests.test_entropy_bound
```

The [literature audit](entropy-literature-audit-2026-09-21.md) identifies
known ingredients and limits the novelty claim. The
[finite permutation route](entropy-finite-revelation.md) is the current
formalization plan: separation, exact support inclusion, and the
fixed-order counting inequality have Lean proofs. Random-permutation
counts, the logarithmic bound, and final composition remain open formal
obligations. The full general theorem and its novelty still require
review; completed ingredient proofs do not establish that final status.

docs/results.md.content:
# Status: what is established, by what evidence, and what is next

Last updated 2026-09-23 for the complete unconditional Lean bound f(n)<3.178^n.
The earlier proofs, retained checkpoints, and literature review are preserved.
The order-5/order-6 certificate ledger remains as recorded 2026-09-09 (paths updated for the repository layout change,
see the last line of "Numbers behind the ledger"). This is the evidence
ledger of the project: for each claim, the kind of evidence behind it, the
cross-checks that guard against systematic error, and the ordered list of
what remains. It is meant to be updated whenever a claim changes. It is
also the single home of the campaign numbers; other documents point here
rather than repeating them.

## Three kinds of evidence

The repository uses three kinds of evidence, and they are not
interchangeable:

- **Kernel-checked theorem.** A statement verified by the Lean 4 kernel
  from the definitions, resting only on the axioms `propext`,
  `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`. Anyone can re-run the check
  (`lake build`, `#print axioms`).
- **Checked certificate.** A proof of unsatisfiability of a specific
  DIMACS formula, verified by cake_lpr, a checker whose own correctness
  is proved down to machine code. The solver that produced it is not
  trusted; only the checker's verdict is. For the order-6 campaign the
  verdicts are recorded in a journal written by the driver that ran the
  checker (see "What remains outside the kernel" under f(6) = 48).
- **Validated computation.** A program whose output agrees with
  independent programs and known values but has not itself been proved
  correct.

## Claims

### General upper bound: complete unconditional 3.178 theorem

[JointEntropyUpperBound.lean](../lean/SmpMax/General/JointEntropyUpperBound.lean)
proves `stableCount_lt_3178_pow`: for every positive n and strict, complete,
balanced profile I, `stableCount I < (1589/500)^n`. The profile and counting
definitions are unchanged, and the exact public statement is pinned in
`lean/checks/GeneralEntropy.lean`.

The [joint-saving proof](entropy-joint-saving.md) recovers the positive
remainder from simultaneously shrinking both support caps. It handles
coincident witnesses and cross-direction neighbor collisions explicitly.
A third first-step event pays the increased exception-charging costs.
The total entropy saving is n*(2*467/20000+307/500000), with the preceding
gap estimate and twenty-four second-step events unchanged.

The [checkpoint](../results/entropy-joint-saving-2026-09-23/README.md)
retains the full repository check, 112 general theorem audits, separate
kernel replays of all seven new modules, and exact sources. All forty-nine
prior general modules and 187 retained artifacts are preserved. The final
axioms are only `propext`, `Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound`.
No optimality or priority claim follows from this improvement alone.

### Preceding complete 3.18 theorem


[LongerEntropyUpperBound.lean](../lean/SmpMax/General/LongerEntropyUpperBound.lean)
proves `stableCount_lt_318_pow`: for every positive n and every strict,
complete, balanced profile I, `stableCount I < (159/50)^n`. The profile,
stability predicate, and counting function are unchanged. The exact
statement is pinned in `lean/checks/GeneralEntropy.lean`.

The [longer-event proof](entropy-longer-events.md) counts opposite-side
runs j=0,...,23 and covers all twenty-five propagation-witness rows.
A strengthened five-event short-side bound pays the existing charging
costs. Each direction saves at least n*(467/20000), giving a combined
saving of 0.0467 per man in the aggregate entropy bound. Forty-eight
auxiliary labels affect only the reveal order; they add no matching
coordinates. The old finite gap constant is unchanged.

The [checkpoint](../results/entropy-longer-events-2026-09-23/README.md)
retains the full Lean check, the 93 general theorem audits, separate
kernel replays of all nine new modules, exact sources, and preservation
checks for the forty preceding general modules and 179 previous artifacts.
The final theorem uses only `propext`, `Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound`.
Priority and independent specialist review remain open.

### Preceding complete 3.2 theorem


[BidirectionalEntropyUpperBound.lean](../lean/SmpMax/General/BidirectionalEntropyUpperBound.lean)
proves `stableCount_lt_32_pow`: for every positive n and every strict,
complete, balanced profile I, `stableCount I < (16/5)^n`. The only inputs
are n>0 and I. Its axiom list is `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`;
there is no external numerical or UNSAT certificate hypothesis.

The [bidirectional argument](entropy-bidirectional-improvement.md) uses a
common finite padded gap and saves
2*(log(3)/60+log(5/4)/105) per man after summing over all men.
Thirteen additional Lean modules complete the exact event probabilities,
padded support bounds, both matching-level classifications, exception
charging, and aggregate entropy count. The six auxiliary labels affect
only ranks. The counting inequality holds for every injective rank
assignment, so no uniform-restriction lemma is required.

The [formalization checkpoint](../results/entropy-bidirectional-formalization-2026-09-23/README.md)
retains the full repository check, separate kernel replays, exact statement
audit, source snapshots, and preservation checks. The
[formal theorem guide](entropy-lean-proof.md) explains the proof chain.
Priority and independent specialist review remain open.

The [preceding bidirectional checkpoint](../results/entropy-bidirectional-2026-09-23/README.md)
is preserved as the earlier written-proof stage. Its finite validator
checked all 46656 order-three profiles, 500 seeded profiles, and nine
fixtures, including 1407440 real-support queries and both directional
implications. These experiments are corroboration, not assumptions of
the Lean theorem.

The preceding [structural argument](entropy-structural-improvement.md) gives
f(n)<3.272^n for all positive n. A change to a worse stable partner forces
its owner, and then that owner's successor, to change. Four classes of
men yield a uniform saving of log(3)/60 per man from the old log-gap bound.
An exception can charge only its second owner, and each recipient receives
at most two charges. This establishes a smaller base by a new structural
inequality. That earlier written proof is preserved; the stronger 3.2
conclusion is now completely formalized.

Four new modules prove propagation, the abstract counting and weighted
charging lemmas, the short-side entropy saving, and the numerical
comparison with 3.272. Finite checks passed all 46656 order-three profiles,
500 seeded profiles, nine fixtures through order thirteen, and all 50069
maps on sets of size at most six. They performed 1415024 conditional-support
queries and 702807 directional implication checks. These computations
support falsification, not a universal inference from finite examples.
The [structural checkpoint](../results/entropy-structural-2026-09-22/README.md)
retains the exact sources, checked statements, and separate kernel replays.

The [one-sided entropy argument](entropy-upper-bound.md) derives
f(n) <= exp(C*n) for every n >= 1, where
C = sum_{k>=1} 2*log(k)/((k+1)*(k+2)). It uses the alternating-cycle
opposition property to turn already fixed stable pairs into barriers in
each man's stable-partner list. Independent priorities on men give an
exact geometric-gap domination without doubling the number of encoded
coordinates. No size-two-rotation hypothesis is used.

The refined rational-base conclusion f(n)<3.331974^n now has a
[complete Lean proof](entropy-lean-proof.md), including the numerical
comparison. The stronger infinite-series expression exp(C*n) above is
still a written derivation. Priority and external review remain open.
Finite checks cover all 46656
order-three profiles, 500 seeded profiles of orders four through eight,
and eleven saved/generated fixtures through order thirteen. The
[retained evidence](../results/entropy-upper-bound-2026-09-21/README.md)
records which reveal subsets were exhaustive and which were sampled.
The proof's all-order conclusion is not inferred from finite testing.

Twenty core [general Lean modules](../lean/README.md) prove stable-pair
separation, exact support bounds, finite revelation counting, uniform
permutation event counts, the gap tail, a telescoping logarithmic bound,
and the original and refined rational comparisons. That stage established
`SmpMax.General.stableCount_lt_3331974_pow`, with only n>0 and the profile
as inputs. No external numerical-certificate hypothesis is assumed.
The [plan and reflection log](entropy-formalization-plan.md) records the
proof and review stages. The [review packet](entropy-review-2026-09-22.md)
found no definition mismatch in local source review and isolates the
candidate contribution from the established ingredients. The targeted
search located no exact duplicate, without establishing priority.
The [initial literature audit](entropy-literature-audit-2026-09-21.md)
remains available as a dated record. There is no third-party review yet.
The [initial partial checkpoint](../results/entropy-formalization-2026-09-21/README.md)
preserves the earlier six-module state and finite permutation checks.
The [complete checkpoint](../results/entropy-formalization-2026-09-22/README.md)
retains the full successful check output, all seventeen successful kernel
replays, a statement audit, and exact source snapshots. Peak child
resident memory was 1999437824 bytes on the local Mac. The full check
took 29.33 seconds with dependencies already cached.

The [review checkpoint](../results/entropy-review-2026-09-22/README.md)
records a fresh sixteen-theorem signature/axiom audit and confirms that
all 24 proof inputs snapshotted in the complete checkpoint are unchanged.
That review added documentation and evidence, without changing Lean sources.

The later [refinement checkpoint](../results/entropy-refinement-2026-09-22/README.md)
adds three modules proving the sharper finite remainder and the 3.331974
bound; all seventeen earlier general modules are unchanged. The updated
full check passed in 25.185 seconds, with 22 general theorem audits,
the 26 original audits, 300 differential cases, and the existing witness
and LRAT checks. Each new module also passed separate kernel replay.
The [constant analysis](entropy-improvement-limits.md) encloses the
limiting gap-model base between 3.3319739853 and 3.3319739854 using exact
arithmetic and a written tail proof. This is a limit of the relaxation,
not a lower bound on the true maximum count. A base such as 3.3 requires
additional structural information.

The literature reproduction also found a numerical mismatch in the
displayed final series in Claim 24 of Palmer and Palvolgyi. The draft
isolates that specific issue; it does not claim to disprove their main
theorem. The proposed proof above does not depend on that calculation.

### Changed construction rules: no asymptotic improvement found

The [construction-rule batch](construction-rules.md) evaluated 143000
candidates in twelve runs without a scoring-budget skip. A separate
exhaustive check covered all 46656 order-three profiles as uniform product
rules; the maximum after two iterations was 111 at order nine.
Neither search establishes an upper bound on unrestricted instances.

For two particular periodic rules, a complete local transfer graph and
positive integer vector prove count bounds of 107*1.810640^n and
52*1.815104^n at their even orders. A doubled version of the latter has
bound 52*2.11^n at its orders divisible by four. These are all-scale
exclusions of three exact rules, not bounds on f(n) or whole template
classes. The proofs are written combinatorics and exact Python-checked
integer certificates, outside Lean.

The [retained record](../results/construction-rules-2026-09-21/README.md)
contains complete rules, 45 profiles, source snapshots, fresh independent
verification, and transfer certificates. The order-64 controls are checked
by exact classical-profile identity plus the proved recurrence; their
original direct-constraint budget failures remain recorded. No new
extremal record or improved exponential lower bound is claimed.

### Iterated polynomial law and fixed-seed growth limit

The [iterated-lifting proof](iterated-lifting.md) establishes
H_D(I)(x) = (1+x)^n H_I(2x(x+2)/(1+x)^2) for all-size-two seeds, and
proves that this seed class is preserved. It gives an exact recurrence
for every repeated doubling. Every fixed seed in this class has the same
exponential growth base under D, enclosed by the exact rational interval
[2.280142072128, 2.280142072130]. The seed changes a constant factor.
This is a written combinatorial proof, not a Lean theorem or a global
upper bound on f(n); novelty has not been established.

The accompanying five-run search evaluated 160000 candidates and raised
the bounds to f(9) >= 416, f(18) >= 644864, and f(36) >= 1749356055040.
All three have direct rotation and blocking-constraint recounts, and the
order-nine seed also passes brute force. The new order-52 witness has
745131369307463680 stable matchings. Its independent verification route
enumerates the seed polynomial from blocking constraints and applies the
proved recurrence, then compares with direct target rotations. A completed
direct target constraint count at order 52 is not claimed.

The [retained record](../results/iterated-lifting-2026-09-21/README.md)
contains exact proof text, witnesses, source identities, and verification.
The full polynomial identity passes on all 45168 eligible order-three
profiles; the other 1488 profiles have longer rotations and do not satisfy
the hypothesis. Further checks cover 225 random swap profiles, local
projection fibers, and the retained seeds. No asymptotic improvement over
the classical base follows from this construction.

### Weighted-search improvements

The preceding weighted-search batch obtained f(9) >= 412,
f(13) >= 9240, f(18) >= 637088, f(26) >= 378181376, and
f(36) >= 1727165217280. The [weighted-search evidence](../results/weighted-search-2026-09-21/README.md)
includes full preferences, source hashes, and exact reproduction commands.
All witnesses pass rotation and independent blocking-constraint recounts;
the order-nine seed also passes brute force over all 9! matchings.

The 12 completed runs evaluated 420000 candidates without a budget skip.
The [research note](weighted-search.md) explains the exact integer scoring
rule and a checked example in which the smaller base count gives the
larger doubled count. The order-seven and order-eleven starts were not
improved. These remain validated computations, with no upper bound,
worldwide priority claim, or asymptotic improvement asserted. The earlier
bounds and their original evidence are retained below.

### Doubling formula and larger-order lower bounds

The [doubling note](profile-lifting.md) gives an explicit transformation D
at every order and a combinatorial proof of its exact count. For an instance
I whose rotations all have size two, with rotation-poset antichain polynomial
H_P, the formula is s(D(I)) = 2^n H_P(3/2). A weighted version handles
arbitrary rotation lengths. This is a written proof, not a Lean theorem;
novelty of the formula has not been established.

| n | Computational lower bound on f(n) |
|---|---|
| 14 | 24992 |
| 18 | 619904 |
| 26 | 344774528 |
| 28 | 2497797760 |
| 36 | 1681618347520 |

Complete preferences, independent rotation and blocking-constraint recounts,
and source hashes are in the [retained evidence](../results/profile-lifting-2026-09-21/README.md).
Formula validation includes all 46656 order-three profiles, 900 seeded
random profiles, and fixtures with odd and even long rotations. The formula
shares rotation extraction with the first counter; the second counter
uses blocking constraints directly. Comparisons apply the same transformation
to the inspected 2025 construction. Two resource-limited control/extension
runs remain explicitly incomplete. These bounds do not assert exact maxima,
worldwide priority, or an improved asymptotic growth rate.

### f(9) >= 400 and f(13) >= 8546

- **Theorem.** No formal proof object; these are explicit preference
  witnesses checked by exact Python computations.
- **Witnesses.** [Order nine](../results/general-order-2026-09-20/witness-n9-400.json)
  has exactly 400 stable matchings; [order thirteen](../results/general-order-2026-09-20/witness-n13-8546.json)
  has exactly 8546. Preference permutations and legal saved schedules are
  checked, including agreement with the campaign's independent read-off.
- **Independent counts.** Rotation extraction and memoized downset counting
  agree with a separate blocking-pair constraint counter. At order nine,
  the original brute-force counter checks all 362880 permutations as well.
  [Verification transcript](../results/general-order-2026-09-20/verification.json).
- **Identity and reproduction.** Exact commands, seeds, initial profiles,
  generating source hashes, base commit plus dirty-worktree indication,
  and witness hashes are retained in the [experiment record](../results/general-order-2026-09-20/README.md).
- **Comparison.** The inspected 2025 construction gives 388 and 8048 at
  these orders. This is a comparison with that source, not a completed
  worldwide priority claim; see the [literature audit](literature-2026-09-20.md).
- **What remains outside the kernel.** All counters and their algorithms.
  Extensive cross-checks validate the computations but do not turn them
  into Lean theorems. No exact maximum or asymptotic improvement is claimed.

### Earlier certified results

Each claim below uses the same template: theorem, hypothesis,
certificates, identity checks, corroboration, and what remains outside
the kernel. The two headline claims have the same shape: one Lean theorem
over the definitions at the top of `Faithful.lean` (order 5) and
`SixBridge.lean` (order 6), whose single hypothesis is discharged by
cake_lpr-checked certificates for formulas printed from the Lean
definitions. All Lean files are under `lean/SmpMax/` unless noted.

### f(5) = 16

- **Theorem.** `f5_eq_16_of_unsat` (`lean/SmpMax/Five/ExactMaximum.lean`):
  `(∀ row ∈ perms120, ¬Satisfiable (cubeCNF row)) → (∀ I : Inst, WF I = true → stableCount I ≤ 16) ∧ ∃ I, WF I = true ∧ stableCount I = 16`.
  Zero sorries; axioms `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`. The
  witness is a kernel-only theorem (`lean/checks/FiveWitness.lean`, axiom `propext`
  only).
- **Hypothesis.** The 120 Lean-defined cube formulas `cubeCNF row`,
  `row ∈ perms120`, are unsatisfiable.
- **Certificates.** 120 of 120 cubes, cake_lpr `s VERIFIED UNSAT`
  (`results/f5/lean-cubes/verification.txt`).
- **Identity checks.** The cube formulas are printed from the Lean
  definitions by `lean/ExportFiveCnf.lean`; `docs/verification.md` regenerates
  and re-checks them.
- **Corroboration.** None needed; the whole chain is kernel-checked
  theorem plus checked certificates. (Earlier, independent refutations by
  the direct encoding are recorded in `docs/history/research-notebook.md`.)
- **What remains outside the kernel.** The trust base of `docs/verification.md`:
  the Lean kernel and its three axioms, the definitions at the top of
  `Faithful.lean`, one LRAT checker, and the DIMACS printer.

### f(6) = 48 (upper bound; the theorem also carries the lower bound)

- **Theorem.** `f6_eq_48_of_unsat` (`lean/SmpMax/Six/ExactMaximum.lean`):
  `(∀ c ∈ Cubes6.finalCubes, ¬Satisfiable (Cubes6.cubeFormula 49 c)) → (∀ I : Inst6, WF6 I = true → stableCount6 I ≤ 48) ∧ ∃ I, WF6 I = true ∧ stableCount6 I = 48`.
  Zero sorries; axioms `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`. Inside
  the kernel it composes the reduction (`validity_unconditional` and the
  rest of the 11-file reduction layer, 5,231 lines, 243 theorems), the
  faithfulness layer (`exists_canonical_schedule`, `fits_final`,
  `cube_faithful6`; 19 files, 4,761 lines, 333 theorems, plus the
  2,808-line data file `lean/SmpMax/Six/CampaignSplits.lean` holding the 2,756 recorded split
  decisions that define `finalCubes`) and the witness `dihedral6_count`
  (below).
- **Hypothesis.** The 318,736 cube formulas `cubeFormula 49 c`,
  `c ∈ Cubes6.finalCubes`, are unsatisfiable. `finalCubes` is a Lean
  definition (`Cubes6.lean`, `lean/SmpMax/Six/CampaignSplits.lean`): the leaves of the split
  tree over the 25,493 root cubes of `SchedCNF6.schedCNF49`.
- **Certificates.** All 318,736 leaves: cake_lpr `s VERIFIED UNSAT`,
  0 SAT, `cube_campaign.py --audit` exit 0 (`results/f6/campaign-2026-09-08/audit-complete.txt`;
  provenance and toolchain in `docs/reference/campaign.md`). Journal:
  `results/f6/campaign-2026-09-08/campaign.jsonl.gz`, sha256
  `c9026b08045d8e8824c66d213bfa8eeb5336f118c22e030d42040136be7a8e4e`.
- **Identity checks.** Re-checked for every cube
  (`results/f6/campaign-2026-09-08/lean_identity.txt`): base formula byte-identical to the
  Python writer's; the 25,493 root cubes and all 295,999 split children
  byte-identical; `finalCubes` = the journal's verified set; all 321,492
  journaled formula hashes recomputed from Lean-printed pieces
  (`tools/campaign/verify_lean_hashes.py`). Details in "What guards the f(6) certificate
  layer" below.
- **Corroboration** (validated computation only). The exhaustive
  enumeration of all 26,574,282,886 schedules, maximum 48
  (`experiments/enumeration/enumerate_cycle_schedules.c`); hill-climbing over instances and over
  schedules ([enumeration experiments](../experiments/README.md)). Corroboration, not evidence.
- **What remains outside the kernel.** Item for item the f(5) trust base
  (`docs/verification.md`): the Lean kernel and its three axioms; the definitions
  `Inst6`, `WF6`, `isStable6`, `sms6`, `stableCount6` (about 40 lines at
  the top of `SixBridge.lean`, the one human-checked step); one LRAT
  checker; the printers `lean/ExportSixCnf.lean` and
  `lean/ExportSixCubes.lean` together with the file identity above;
  and the campaign journal. The journal is self-attested: a `verified`
  record is the driver's transcription of cake_lpr's verdict, the
  certificates (about 25 TB) were deleted after checking, and the audit
  checks the records' consistency. Independently verifying a verdict
  means re-solving that cube from the Lean-printed formula (the per-cube
  `cnf_sha256` and `lrat_sha256` make a re-run comparable record by
  record); the whole tree is about 300 core-hours of solver time; a
  205-cube sample has been re-solved independently ("Independent checks"
  below). Lean's `leanchecker` has been run over every module (below).
  Not trusted: solvers, Python scripts, `gen_enum.c`, the plan documents
  (`docs/history/`).

### f(6) ≥ 48

- **Theorem.** `dihedral6_count : stableCount6 dihedral6 = 48`
  (`lean/SmpMax/Six/LowerBound.lean`): the dihedral instance has exactly 48
  stable matchings, by kernel computation (`decide`) over the 720
  permutations. It is the witness half of `f6_eq_48_of_unsat`.
- **Hypothesis.** None.
- **Certificates.** None needed.
- **Identity checks.** The instance is a Lean literal (`dihedral6`); its
  ranking matrix is displayed in `docs/f6.md`.
- **Corroboration.** The same instance recounted at 48 by three
  independent programs (`tools/stable_matchings.py`, `tools/rotation_poset.py`,
  `sched_sat.readoff_counts` in `tools/schedule_encoding.py`).
- **What remains outside the kernel.** Nothing beyond the kernel, the
  three axioms and the definitions at the top of `SixBridge.lean`.

### f(7) ≥ 85

- **Theorem.** None; this is a validated computation, not a proof object.
- **Hypothesis.** —
- **Certificates.** —
- **Identity checks.** The two instances are re-derived byte-identically
  from their schedules (`python3 experiments/search/search_swap_schedules.py 7 <seed> <seconds>`,
  re-done 2026-09-08).
- **Corroboration.** Two explicit instances (`results/f7/witnesses-85.txt`), each counted
  at 85 by brute force, by an explicit all-blocking-pairs recount, and via
  the rotation poset's downsets; the search runs behind the claims are

- **What remains outside the kernel.** Everything: three unproved
  counting programs agreeing with each other.

### A344669(3,4,5) = 1092 / 144 / 507,254,400

- **Theorem.** None.
- **Hypothesis.** —
- **Certificates.** —
- **Identity checks.** —
- **Corroboration.** Independent recount: brute force over all 46,656

  (`experiments/enumeration/enumerate_f5_profiles.py`; the n = 5 per-cube counts in `results/f5/profile-enumeration.txt`,
  the n = 3 and n = 4 confirmations recorded in `docs/history/research-notebook.md`),

## What guards the f(6) certificate layer against systematic error

1. **Single source of truth for the formula and the cubes.** The CNF is
   defined in Lean (`lean/SmpMax/Six/ScheduleEncoding.lean`, a line-by-line
   transcription of `tools/schedule_encoding.py`) and printed by `export_sched_cnf`
   (`lean/ExportSixCnf.lean`); the root cubes, the split children
   and the certified cube set `finalCubes` are Lean definitions
   (`Cubes6.lean`, `lean/SmpMax/Six/CampaignSplits.lean`) printed by `export_cubes6`
   (`lean/ExportSixCubes.lean`). The theorem quantifies over these
   definitions, not over any Python object.
2. **Every formula re-derived.** The Lean output is byte-identical to the
   Python writer's for the base formula (sha256 `28421fb6…`, 84,882
   variables, 2,709,212 clauses), and all 321,492 journaled `cnf_sha256`
   values (hashed by the driver before solving) recompute from the
   Lean-printed header, base body and unit clauses (`tools/campaign/verify_lean_hashes.py`,
   `matched=321492 mismatched=0`; transcript `results/f6/campaign-2026-09-08/lean_identity.txt`).
3. **Cube-set identity.** `canonicalCubes2` prints the driver's 25,493
   root ids byte-identically; `extendCanon` prints the 295,999 children of
   all 2,756 journaled splits byte-identically; `finalCubes` prints
   exactly the 318,736 `verified` ids.
4. **The audit.** `tools/campaign/cube_campaign.py --audit` recomputes the root set,
   checks that every root is `verified` or `split` with all children
   recursively covered, and checks every verified record's fields: solver
   rc 20, the driver-derived `cake_verified` boolean (defined at write
   time as `s VERIFIED UNSAT` in cake_lpr's output and not killed) with
   `cake_rc 0`, no kill flag, well-formed hashes. Final verdict:
   `roots=25493 nodes=321492 verified=318736 missing=0 bad=0 header_problems=0`
   (`results/f6/campaign-2026-09-08/audit-complete.txt`; the earlier main-run audit is
   `results/f6/campaign-2026-09-08/audit-before-retries.txt`). It is a consistency check of the
   journal, not a re-check of any certificate.
5. **Positive control (encoding not vacuous).** With the dihedral
   schedule pinned
   (`--prefix` `0,1;2,3;4,5;1,2;0,5;3,4;0,1;2,3;4,5;1,2;0,5;3,4;0,1;2,3;4,5`),
   the formula at k = 48 is satisfiable; the model decodes to exactly that
   schedule with 48 distinct selected matchings and an independent recount
   of the read-off gives 48; the same cube at k = 49 is unsatisfiable
   (re-run 2026-09-08 with pysat/CaDiCaL).
6. **Agreement across unrelated methods.** The certificate campaign,
   the direct enumeration of the schedule space
   (`experiments/enumeration/enumerate_cycle_schedules.c`), and hill-climbing over instances and
   over schedules (> 10^9 evaluations; `experiments/search/search_instances.py`,
   `struct_hunt.py`, `relaxed_search.py`) all top out at 48; the same
   machinery reproduces f(3), f(4), f(5) = 3, 10, 16, the last against
   this repository's own certified theorem.

The driver's pilot runs (dry run, fix check, depth-3 probe, CaDiCaL
checks) are in `results/f6/campaign-2026-09-08/` (the named probe files); the scripts that ran and monitored
the campaign are in `docs/history/container-scripts/` (archived shell scripts) and `tools/campaign/` (maintained tools). Neither directory is on the
evidence path.

## Independent checks (2026-09-09)

1. **Re-solve of a random cube sample with the pinned toolchain, on a
   second machine.** 205 verified cubes (stratified by depth and
   closedness; 164 originally solved on the Mac mini, 34 on the M4 Max
   laptop, 7 on the x86-64 container) were re-solved on another Mac from a
   fresh clone, with CaDiCaL rebuilt at commit `c6073042` and cake_lpr
   built from the hash-checked `cake_lpr_arm8.S` (`95b64883…`): 205 / 205
   verified (`s VERIFIED UNSAT`), 205 / 205 `cnf_sha256` equal to the
   journal, 204 / 205 `lrat_sha256` equal (all 198 arm64-origin records
   byte-identical; one of the 7 container-origin records has a different
   proof trace of the same formula, same verdict, an architecture/compiler
   effect). `results/f6/campaign-2026-09-08/recheck_2026-09-09.txt` and the new journal
   `results/f6/campaign-2026-09-08/recheck_2026-09-09.jsonl` record commands, hashes and
   times (263 s wall for the sample). This confirms the journal's
   self-report on the sample; it does not replace re-solving the other
   318,531 cubes. The recipe (`cube_campaign.py --solver cadical --force
   ... --cubes <ids>`, then compare `cnf_sha256` / `lrat_sha256` per cube
   with the journal's last record for that cube) is the "Reproduce" block
   of `results/f6/campaign-2026-09-08/recheck_2026-09-09.txt`, also given in `docs/verification.md`.
2. **`leanchecker` over the development.** Lean 4.33.1's built-in
   `leanchecker` replayed every declaration of all 37 imported modules and
   the root module through the kernel on 2026-09-09: 38 / 38 clean (silent
   exit 0), about 8 s per module; a nonexistent module name errors, so the
   tool was live (`results/f6/campaign-2026-09-08/leanchecker_2026-09-09.txt`).

## Remaining work

The [roadmap](roadmap.md) lists publication, third-party re-checking and
larger-order research. [Publishing instructions](publishing.md) retain the
draft release state. No license is selected for this checkout.

# Remaining work

The order-5 and order-6 formal proofs are complete with explicit UNSAT
hypotheses. The [evidence ledger](results.md) records what has been checked.

1. **Review the complete 3.178 theorem and its attribution.**
   The [Lean theorem](entropy-lean-proof.md) now proves f(n)<3.178^n for every
   positive n, including the exact event probabilities, actual support
   bounds, both directional charging sums, and the numerical comparison.
   The [written proof](entropy-joint-saving.md) explains the
   same argument. Obtain an independent reading, complete the
   forward-citation check, and prepare a manuscript around the reviewed
   claim. The [review packet](entropy-review-2026-09-22.md) preserves the
   earlier definition audit and literature comparison; it should be
   extended to the new structural steps before claiming priority.
   The earlier [3.272 proof](entropy-structural-improvement.md) and
   [constant analysis](entropy-improvement-limits.md) remain available.
   The infinite-series expression in the [original draft](entropy-upper-bound.md)
   is an optional further formalization. Follow the
   [small plans and reflections](entropy-formalization-plan.md).
   No reviewer has been contacted and no publication has been made.
2. **Prepare the evidence release.** Review the draft release, choose a
   license before publication, obtain persistent identifiers, and prepare
   arXiv and OEIS submissions. The checkout remains unlicensed by the owner's
   choice. [Publishing instructions](publishing.md) and [OEIS drafts](oeis-draft.md)
   preserve the release preparation already completed.
3. **Obtain a third-party certificate re-check.** The whole order-6 tree
   takes about 300 core-hours. The [verification guide](verification.md)
   covers the existing 205-cube sample and full-run requirements.
4. **Go beyond fixed-seed doubling.** The [polynomial transformation and
   growth proof](iterated-lifting.md) determine the limit of this construction:
   every fixed swap-only seed has the same exponential base. Test a changed
   local construction or a controlled family of varying seeds. Finite
   improvements and proof-based witnesses now extend through order 52.
   Follow the [research plan](general-order-research.md) and complete the
   priority review before claiming a new construction theorem. The
   [asymptotic target](asymptotic-target.md) gives an exact success test,
   the finite-witness route, and the next construction experiments.
   The [first rule-search batch](construction-rules.md) found no improvement
   and proved upper bounds for three specific periodic rules. Use the
   transfer method to assess repeatable growth in further candidates.
5. **Investigate the size-2 extremality conjecture.** The order-7 data
   support a conjecture, not an upper-bound proof; see the [order-7 guide](f7.md).

The [layout validation](layout-verification.md) records the preservation
checks for this reorganization. The [order-6 design record](design/f6-faithfulness.md)
describes completed obligations and their original lemma numbering.

# Verification guide

Run the commands below from the repository root. The checks progress from
saved witnesses to formal statements, formula identity, and freshly checked
SAT certificates. The [evidence ledger](results.md) records the original runs.

| Check | Establishes | Typical cost |
|---|---|---|
| Witness recount | Lower bounds 16, 48, 85 and 85 | Seconds |
| Lean build and axioms | General 3.178 bound; both fixed-order exact-maximum theorems conditional on UNSAT | Initial dependency download and build: about 20–30 minutes |
| Campaign identity and audit | Complete cube coverage and every recorded formula hash | A few minutes after building |
| Order-5 certificates | Independently checks all 120 upper-bound cubes | About 2–3 hours |
| Order-6 certificates | Independently checks selected or all upper-bound cubes | Minutes for the 205-cube sample; about 300 core-hours for the full tree |

## Prerequisites

- macOS or Linux, Python 3.9 or later, and Git.
- [elan](https://github.com/leanprover/elan) for Lean. The toolchain and
  Mathlib versions are pinned in `lean/`; allow roughly 8 GB for dependencies.
- Solvers and cake_lpr only for certificate regeneration. See the
  [pinned toolchain instructions](reference/solver-toolchain.md).

The verification tools use the Python standard library. Alternative
experiments requiring PySAT use `requirements-experiments.txt`.
Generated output goes under the ignored `runs/` directory.

## 1. Check witnesses and saved files

```bash
python3 tools/verify_witnesses.py
python3 tools/check_artifacts.py
python3 tools/check_docs.py
```

Expected witness counts: **16, 48, 85, 85**. The verifier compares complete
matching sets from two counters, checks rotation-poset downset counts, and
reconstructs the order-7 preferences from their schedules. These establish
lower bounds. Artifact hashes establish file identity, not mathematical validity.

## 2. Build and inspect the Lean statements

```bash
(cd lean && lake exe cache get)
bash tools/check_lean.sh
```

This builds the library and all three exporters, rejects `sorry`, and checks
26 theorem axiom lists, including `f5_eq_16_of_unsat` and `f6_eq_48_of_unsat`.
Each uses exactly `propext`, `Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound`. It also
checks the standalone order-5 witness (only `propext`), 300 differential
count cases (zero mismatches), and the order-4 LRAT pilot.

The same script separately audits 112 general-order theorems
from [GeneralEntropy.lean](../lean/checks/GeneralEntropy.lean), allowing
only subsets of those three standard axioms. These include the complete
theorem `stableCount_lt_3178_pow`, the preserved earlier bounds, exact
relative-order counts, local directional savings, and matching-level charging.
The general theorems have no external UNSAT or
numerical-certificate hypothesis. Its [scope and proof map](entropy-lean-proof.md)
distinguish it from the original infinite-series refinement.

The two fixed-order statements have the same shape: if all specified Lean-defined CNFs
are unsatisfiable, the maximum is exactly 16 or 48. For order 5 there are
120 formulas; for order 6 there are 318,736 leaf formulas. The order-6
normalization, encoding faithfulness and cube coverage proofs are complete.
The [Lean guide](../lean/README.md) gives the statements and reading order.

Read the definitions of instances, well-formedness, stability and counting
in [Five/Definitions.lean](../lean/SmpMax/Five/Definitions.lean) and
[Six/ReadOff.lean](../lean/SmpMax/Six/ReadOff.lean) to confirm that the
formal statements express the intended stable-marriage problem.
For the general theorem, review the small definitions in
[General/Definitions.lean](../lean/SmpMax/General/Definitions.lean): each
rank row and matching is a permutation, stability excludes every blocking
pair, and the count includes all stable matching permutations.

Optional kernel replay of every imported module, from the repository root:

```bash
cd lean
python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
modules = [line.split()[1] for line in Path('SmpMax.lean').read_text().splitlines()
           if line.startswith('import SmpMax.')]
for module in [*modules, 'SmpMax']:
    subprocess.run(['lake', 'env', 'leanchecker', module], check=True)
print(f'{len(modules) + 1} modules replayed successfully')
PY
```

## 3. Audit the campaign and check every formula

```bash
mkdir -p runs/f6
gzip -dc results/f6/campaign-2026-09-08/campaign.jsonl.gz > runs/f6/campaign.jsonl
python3 tools/campaign/check_lean_identity.py --journal runs/f6/campaign.jsonl
```

The helper invokes the current Lean exporters and compares their output
with the journal and Python cube definitions. Every mismatch causes failure.
Expected results:

- Audit: **321,492** distinct cubes, **318,736** verified, **2,756** split;
  zero missing or bad records and `audit: OK`.
- Exactly **25,493** roots and **295,999** children of the recorded splits.
- `Cubes6.finalCubes`: **318,736** unique IDs, equal to the verified set.
- All **321,492** recorded formula hashes match; zero missing unit lists.

The base CNF hash is
`28421fb68b0f494b99d1918aa64cff248443161dc7a6c220e0c3e895a67df59b`.
Outputs, complete ID lists and a JSON summary are in `runs/f6/lean-identity/`.
For the low-level recipe, see the exporters in the [Lean guide](../lean/README.md).
The original [identity transcript](../results/f6/campaign-2026-09-08/lean_identity.txt)
uses historical paths; the [migration map](path-migration.md) resolves them.

Source hashes in the journal identify the original scripts. Moving imports
and changing documentation changes a source hash without changing the
formula. The audit reports that difference as provenance; formula mismatch
is a failure. The full identity check above independently checks the formulas.

## 4. Regenerate the order-5 certificates

Install kissat 4.0.4 on `PATH`, drat-trim (historical commit `2e3b2dc`) at
`dt-src/drat-trim`, and cake_lpr at `cake_lpr-src/cake_lpr`. The
[toolchain reference](reference/solver-toolchain.md) covers cake_lpr;
the other sources are [kissat](https://github.com/arminbiere/kissat) and
[drat-trim](https://github.com/marijnheule/drat-trim).

```bash
python3 tools/verify_five_cubes.py
```

The runner exports the Lean formulas, requires solver exit 20 (UNSAT),
checks DRAT and LRAT verdicts, and records formula/proof hashes before
deleting successful proof files. Failures stop the run and retain artifacts.
Use `--keep-proofs` to archive certificates. A successful full run ends
with `Verified 120/120 cubes in this run. All upper-bound cubes checked.`

To inspect formulas without solving:

```bash
python3 tools/verify_five_cubes.py --export-only
```

Files go to `runs/f5/lean-cubes/`: 120 production CNFs, 120 positive
controls and `perms120.txt`. Concatenated in filename order, the production
CNFs hash to `044d0edbd9762166d925038056b3ef9ed762293d3f7637055e1105d1eca30ec6`;
all 240 hash to `a93f5e58cd23976b303e26f5dd2fcd4ab66f91797b0b02bd2bfba13887c6a2ef`.
The positive control `cubeL16_105.cnf` must be SAT.

## 5. Regenerate order-6 certificates

Follow [solver setup and sample re-solving](reference/solver-toolchain.md).
It includes a positive control and the exact 205-cube sample recorded in
the repository. For each re-solved cube, require a valid checker verdict
and the same CNF hash. A different proof hash can reflect a different solver
build; it still needs independent acceptance by the checker.

The [campaign reference](reference/campaign.md) covers a complete run.
Use the verified ID list produced in step 3 to reproduce the existing
leaf set. A sample does not discharge the full UNSAT hypothesis.

## What remains trusted

The formal side relies on Lean's kernel, the three listed axioms, and the
human interpretation of the problem definitions. The certificate side
relies on the DIMACS printers, formula identity, a sound LRAT checker and
its execution environment. The solvers supply certificates to that checker.

The stored order-6 journal is self-attested: it records the driver's
transcription of checker verdicts. About 25 TB of certificates were deleted.
Auditing the journal and recomputing hashes do not re-check those certificates;
fresh solving and checking are required for independent verification.
The saved 205-cube second-machine check does not cover the whole tree.
Order-5 certificates were also not archived and can be regenerated in step 4.

lean/README.md.content:
# The Lean development

One Lake package, `SmpMax`, contains the general 3.178 upper bound and
the order-5 and order-6 proofs.
Modules are grouped under `SmpMax/Five/` and `SmpMax/Six/`; new arbitrary-order
ingredients live under `SmpMax/General/`. Lean 4 `v4.33.1`
with Mathlib (`lake exe cache get` fetches the prebuilt cache, about 8 GB
under `.lake/`). `lake build` kernel-checks every theorem; `grep -rn sorry SmpMax/` is empty. Sizes and theorem counts per
layer: `docs/results.md` ("Numbers behind the ledger").

## The two fixed-order exact-maximum theorems

Both rest on the axioms `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound` and
nothing else; both have exactly one hypothesis, discharged outside the
kernel by cake_lpr-checked UNSAT certificates for formulas printed from
the Lean definitions by the exporters below.

`SmpMax/Five/ExactMaximum.lean`:

```lean
theorem f5_eq_16_of_unsat
    (H : ∀ row ∈ perms120, ¬ Satisfiable (cubeCNF row)) :
    (∀ I : Inst, WF I = true → stableCount I ≤ 16) ∧
    (∃ I : Inst, WF I = true ∧ stableCount I = 16)
```

`SmpMax/Six/ExactMaximum.lean`:

```lean
theorem f6_eq_48_of_unsat
    (H : ∀ c ∈ Cubes6.finalCubes, ¬ Satisfiable (Cubes6.cubeFormula 49 c)) :
    (∀ I : Inst6, WF6 I = true → stableCount6 I ≤ 48) ∧
    (∃ I : Inst6, WF6 I = true ∧ stableCount6 I = 48)
```

The definitions the statements quantify over are the one human-checked
step: `Inst`, `WF`, `isStable`, `stableCount` at the top of
`SmpMax/Five/Definitions.lean` (order 5) and `Inst6`, `WF6`, `isStable6`, `sms6`,
`stableCount6` at the top of `SmpMax/Six/ReadOff.lean` (order 6), about
forty lines each. `perms120` and `cubeCNF` (`SmpMax/Five/Encoding.lean`), and
`Cubes6.finalCubes` and `Cubes6.cubeFormula` (`SmpMax/Six/CampaignCubes.lean`,
`SmpMax/Six/CampaignSplits.lean`), are Lean definitions; the identity between what they
print and what the certificate campaigns refuted is documented in
`docs/verification.md` and, for order 6, `results/f6/campaign-2026-09-08/lean_identity.txt`.

## Module map

The main proof modules live in `SmpMax/`; `SmpMax.lean` imports all 93 of them. The
tables group the modules by layer; a module depends only on modules
above it and on Mathlib (the exact import order is `SmpMax.lean`). Every module has a `/-! # ... -/` header
docstring that is more detailed than the line here; the faithfulness
files cite the section and lemma numbers of the archived plan
`docs/design/f6-faithfulness.md`.

### Order-5 core

| module | what it proves |
|---|---|
| [Five/Definitions.lean](SmpMax/Five/Definitions.lean) | Defines 5 × 5 instances as rank tables (`Inst`, `WF`), stability (`isStable`) and the count (`stableCount`); proves the covering step `cube_covering` (man 1's ranking is one of the 120 permutations). |
| [Five/Symmetry.lean](SmpMax/Five/Symmetry.lean) | `relabel I` renames women by man 0's rank row; well-formedness is preserved and the count unchanged, giving `reduce_man0'` (WLOG man 0 ranks the identity). |
| [Five/Encoding.lean](SmpMax/Five/Encoding.lean) | `cubeCNF row`, the selector-style cube formula for order 5 at 17 slots (`cubeCNF16` at 16 for the positive control), and `Satisfiable`; the single source of truth for what `export_cnf` prints. |
| [Five/EncodingFaithfulness.lean](SmpMax/Five/EncodingFaithfulness.lean) | The assignment `tau I idxs` read off an instance and its stable matchings, the literal-evaluation lemmas, and `cube_faithful'`: an instance in cube `row` with at least 17 stable matchings satisfies `cubeCNF row`. |
| [Five/UpperBound.lean](SmpMax/Five/UpperBound.lean) | `f5_upper_of_unsat`: combines `reduce_man0'`, `cube_covering` and `cube_faithful` into f(5) ≤ 16 conditional on the 120 refutations. |
| [Five/ExactMaximum.lean](SmpMax/Five/ExactMaximum.lean) | The 16-matching witness `witnessI`, its count by kernel `decide` (via `List.permutations'`), and the combined statement `f5_eq_16_of_unsat`. |
| `checks/FiveWitness.lean` | Standalone file outside the package: the same witness recounted with no imports, axiom `propext` only (`lake env lean checks/FiveWitness.lean`). |

### Order-6 reduction (11 files)

From "every well-formed order-6 instance" to "some legal schedule's
read-off instance, encoded as a fixed CNF". End statement:
`validity_unconditional` (`Six/NormalizeMatching`).

| module | what it proves |
|---|---|
| [Six/ReadOff.lean](SmpMax/Six/ReadOff.lean) | Defines order-6 instances, stability and the count (`Inst6`, `WF6`, `isStable6`, `sms6`, `stableCount6`); `readoff I` promotes stable partners to the top of each list; the bridge lemma `bridge : stableCount6 I ≤ stableCount6 (readoff I)`. |
| [Six/Lattice.lean](SmpMax/Six/Lattice.lean) | The stable-matching lattice: `meetM I μ ν` (each man's better partner) is again stable; the man-optimal and woman-optimal matchings; the inverse-permutation toolkit `invMatch`. |
| [Six/Chains.lean](SmpMax/Six/Chains.lean) | `theChain I`, an explicit maximal chain from `manOpt I` to `womanOpt I` by minimum-rank-sum dominators; `chain_complete`, `traj_mem_iff`, `wtraj_nodup`, `total_moves_le_30`: the trajectories are exactly the stable partners in preference order, without repetition, within the 30-move budget. |
| [Six/Relabeling.lean](SmpMax/Six/Relabeling.lean) | Relabeling men and women by the same permutation preserves the identity matching, maps schedules to schedules and leaves `stableCount6` invariant (Lemma sym (ii)). |
| [Six/Schedule.lean](SmpMax/Six/Schedule.lean) | Schedules as lists of cyclic steps applied from the identity matching; trajectories as destuttered partner columns; the read-off instance `readoffS` (women's trajectories reversed, canonical bottom completion) and legality `Legal`. |
| [Six/OrderPreservingBridge.lean](SmpMax/Six/OrderPreservingBridge.lean) | `count_le_of_orderPreserving`: the bridge lemma in bottom-agnostic form, for any instance ranking stable partners on top in the original order. |
| [Six/CycleDecomposition.lean](SmpMax/Six/CycleDecomposition.lean) | Cycle structure of one matching step: `prevOwner` is injective, so a moved man's orbit returns within six steps (makes fuel-6 orbit extraction total and correct). |
| [Six/ChainToSchedule.lean](SmpMax/Six/ChainToSchedule.lean) | `chainSched I` concatenates the single-step decompositions of consecutive chain elements into one schedule whose matching sequence passes through the whole chain: the executable Validity Lemma. |
| [Six/ScheduleDominance.lean](SmpMax/Six/ScheduleDominance.lean) | `sc_le_readoffS_chainSched`: `stableCount6 I ≤ stableCount6 (readoffS (chainSched I))` when the man-optimal matching is the identity, via the bottom-agnostic bridge. |
| [Six/NormalizeMatching.lean](SmpMax/Six/NormalizeMatching.lean) | Women-only relabeling `wrelabel6` sends the man-optimal matching to the identity (`manOpt_wrelabel6`) without changing the count; hence `validity_unconditional`: every well-formed order-6 instance is dominated by the read-off of some `Legal` schedule. |
| [Six/ScheduleEncoding.lean](SmpMax/Six/ScheduleEncoding.lean) | The schedule CNF `schedCNF k` (and `schedCNFn n k`, `cubeCNF k prefix`), a line-by-line transcription of `tools/schedule_encoding.py :: build(6, k)` with the Python variable numbering; the single source of truth for what `export_sched_cnf` prints. |

### Order-6 faithfulness (19 files plus the data file `Six/CampaignSplits`)

From "some legal schedule reads off at least 49 stable matchings" to "some
cube of `finalCubes` has a satisfiable formula". Chain in `Six/ExactMaximum`:
`exists_canonical_schedule` → `fits_final` → `cube_faithful6`.

| module | what it proves |
|---|---|
| [Six/CampaignCubes.lean](SmpMax/Six/CampaignCubes.lean) | Campaign cubes as prefixes of min-first shapes plus a `stopped` flag; `canonicalCubes2` (the driver's `root_cubes(2)`), `extendCanon` (its `split_children`), the first-appearance rule `canonAtB`, the legality filter `legalPrefixB`; `CubeWF`, `Fits`, `cubeFormula`. Computable, so `export_cubes6` can print them. |
| [Six/VariableDecoding.lean](SmpMax/Six/VariableDecoding.lean) | `dec6 k v` inverts the variable numbering of `Six/ScheduleEncoding`; the decode lemmas `dec_*` (`SchedCNF6.dec_pwVar3` is the last) return each offset function's arguments. |
| [Six/TrajectoryPrefixes.lean](SmpMax/Six/TrajectoryPrefixes.lean) | Position lemmas connecting a partner column's prefixes (what the visited masks read) with first-occurrence positions in its destuttered trajectory (what the read-off ranks read). |
| [Six/CyclicShapes.lean](SmpMax/Six/CyclicShapes.lean) | Rotating a step to min-first form (`minFirst`) changes neither the matching sequence nor legality (`Legal_map_minFirst`); every legal step is an entry of `cyclicShapes 6` (`minFirst_mem_cyclicShapes`); `permsN6_perm_permutations` relates the formula's 720 matchings to Mathlib's permutations. |
| [Six/FrameAssignment.lean](SmpMax/Six/FrameAssignment.lean) | The CNF state at frame `t` (`frame S t`, visited mask `vis`) and the witness assignment `tau6 k S idxs` / `τV`, which assigns every decoded variable by the gate formula the Python encoder uses for it. |
| [Six/ReadOffSemantics.lean](SmpMax/Six/ReadOffSemantics.lean) | The crux `PM_sem` / `PW_sem`: under `τV` the men's and women's preference variables are true exactly when the read-off row orders the two partners that way. |
| [Six/ScheduleLength.lean](SmpMax/Six/ScheduleLength.lean) | `Legal_length_le_15`: a legal order-6 schedule has at most 15 steps (the frame bound that fixes the formula's size); the per-man cap and the 30-move budget checked by the driver. |
| [Six/ScheduleRelabeling.lean](SmpMax/Six/ScheduleRelabeling.lean) | `relabelSched σ S` renames the men of every step; equivariance, `Legal_relabel`, and the count bridge `sc_le_readoffS_relabelSched`, re-instantiated at the relabeled instance because `readoffS` is not relabel-equivariant (plan L3.1–L3.7, L3.12–L3.16). |
| [Six/FirstAppearance.lean](SmpMax/Six/FirstAppearance.lean) | First-appearance normalization: `partOrder`, `sigmaOf`, and `firstApp_relabel`: under `sigmaOf S` every step of `S` is first-appearance canonical; rotation invariance of `canonAtB` (plan L3.8–L3.11, L3.21, L4.14). |
| [Six/PrefixLegality.lean](SmpMax/Six/PrefixLegality.lean) | Prefixes of legal schedules are legal (`Legal_take`) and pass the driver's cube filter (`legalPrefixB_of_Legal`); matching sequences and trajectories of a prefix are prefixes (plan L5.10–L5.12). |
| [Six/StateClauses.lean](SmpMax/Six/StateClauses.lean) | Clause families 1–3 hold under `tau6`: `init_sat`, `matching_sat`, `step_sat` (initial state, matching one-hot, step one-hot). |
| [Six/GateClauses.lean](SmpMax/Six/GateClauses.lean) | Clause families 5–9, the definitional gates, hold under `tau6` for every schedule: `before_sat`, `neither_sat`, `pm_sat`, `beforeW_sat`, `pw_sat`, via generic gate lemmas on the exact literal patterns of `Six/ScheduleEncoding`. |
| [Six/TransitionClauses.lean](SmpMax/Six/TransitionClauses.lean) | Clause family 4, the transition clauses, holds for a legal schedule: `stopTrans_sat`, `shapeClauses_sat`, `noRevisit_sat` (from `noRevisit_sem`, plan L5.9), `visUpdate_sat`, assembled as `transition_sat`. |
| [Six/SelectionClauses.lean](SmpMax/Six/SelectionClauses.lean) | Clause families 10–12 hold: `selector_sat`, `ladder_sat` (strictly increasing selections), `block_sat6` (a selected matching admits no blocking pair, via `PM_sem` / `PW_sem`); the index list `idxsOf` of a read-off's stable matchings and `stableCount6_eq_filter_permsN`. |
| [Six/CubeUnits.lean](SmpMax/Six/CubeUnits.lean) | The cube's unit clauses hold under the witness assignment: `prefixUnits_sat`, `stopUnits_sat`; `cubeFormula_sat_of` packages base formula plus units. |
| [Six/LowerBound.lean](SmpMax/Six/LowerBound.lean) | The dihedral Latin instance `dihedral6` (OEIS A351413) and `dihedral6_count : stableCount6 dihedral6 = 48` by kernel `decide` over the 720 permutations; `f6_lower`. |
| [Six/CampaignSplits.lean](SmpMax/Six/CampaignSplits.lean) | Data generated from the journal: the ids of the depth-2 and depth-3 cubes the campaign split (`isSplitDepth2`, `isSplitDepth3`) and `finalCubes := refineCubes (refineCubes canonicalCubes2 isSplitDepth2) isSplitDepth3`, the certified cube set (numbers: `docs/results.md`). |
| [Six/CubeCoverage.lean](SmpMax/Six/CubeCoverage.lean) | Every legal first-appearance canonical schedule fits a well-formed cube of `finalCubes` (`fits_final`), from `cube_of_canonical` (a root cube fits), `fits_refine` (fitting survives a split round, for any split predicate) and the `*_WF` lemmas (plan L3.17–L3.20). |
| [Six/EncodingFaithfulness.lean](SmpMax/Six/EncodingFaithfulness.lean) | `schedCNF_sat` (the twelve family lemmas assembled), `cube_faithful6` (a legal schedule of at most 15 steps whose read-off has at least 49 stable matchings makes every fitting well-formed cube satisfiable at target 49), `exists_canonical_schedule` (from `49 ≤ stableCount6 I` to such a schedule, via `validity_unconditional`, `sigmaOf` and the count chain) and `f6_upper_of_unsat_of_coverage`. |
| [Six/ExactMaximum.lean](SmpMax/Six/ExactMaximum.lean) | `f6_upper_of_unsat` (coverage discharged by `fits_final`) and `f6_eq_48_of_unsat` (adds `f6_lower`). |

### The 1 + 25 theorems CI checks

`.github/workflows/lean-verify.yml` prints the axioms of
`f5_eq_16_of_unsat` and of 25 order-6 theorems and requires
`[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]` for each; `docs/verification.md`
explains the trust boundary; the module map above describes each theorem. By file:
`bridge` (Six/ReadOff); `chain_complete`, `traj_mem_iff`, `wtraj_nodup`,
`total_moves_le_30` (Six/Chains, on the toolkit of Six/Lattice); `count_le_of_orderPreserving`
(Six/OrderPreservingBridge); `sc_le_readoffS_chainSched` (Six/ScheduleDominance);
`manOpt_wrelabel6`, `validity_unconditional` (Six/NormalizeMatching); `PM_sem`,
`PW_sem` (Six/ReadOffSemantics); `Legal_length_le_15` (Six/ScheduleLength);
`minFirst_mem_cyclicShapes`, `permsN6_perm_permutations`,
`Legal_map_minFirst` (Six/CyclicShapes); `SchedCNF6.dec_pwVar3` (Six/VariableDecoding);
`firstApp_relabel` (Six/FirstAppearance); `Legal_relabel`,
`sc_le_readoffS_relabelSched` (Six/ScheduleRelabeling);
`exists_canonical_schedule`, `cube_faithful6` (Six/EncodingFaithfulness);
`fits_final` (Six/CubeCoverage); `dihedral6_count` (Six/LowerBound);
`f6_upper_of_unsat`, `f6_eq_48_of_unsat` (Six/ExactMaximum). CI also checks that
`checks/FiveWitness.lean` depends on `[propext]` alone.

### General entropy theorem

These fifty-six general modules are independent of the fixed-order proofs.
They include the complete 3.178 counting theorem and preserve the earlier
3.332, 3.331974, 3.2, and 3.18 proofs.
[JointEntropyUpperBound.lean](SmpMax/General/JointEntropyUpperBound.lean) proves:

```lean
theorem stableCount_lt_3178_pow {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (I : Profile n) :
    (stableCount I : ℝ) < (1589 / 500 : ℝ) ^ n
```

There is no external certificate hypothesis. The
[formal theorem guide](../docs/entropy-lean-proof.md) explains the scope,
and the [plan and reflection log](../docs/entropy-formalization-plan.md)
records the construction. The [review packet](../docs/entropy-review-2026-09-22.md)
contains the local interpretation audit and literature comparison;
priority and independent review remain open.

| Module | Completed content |
|---|---|
| [General/Definitions.lean](SmpMax/General/Definitions.lean) | Arbitrary-n strict complete rank profiles, bijective matchings, stability, compatible families, exact support, and counts. |
| [General/Separation.lean](SmpMax/General/Separation.lean) | Classical opposition and stable-pair separation, without global dominance or rotation restrictions. |
| [General/Barriers.lean](SmpMax/General/Barriers.lean) | Revealed coordinates fix inverse partners and preserve the side of every stable-partner barrier. |
| [General/PartnerIntervals.lean](SmpMax/General/PartnerIntervals.lean) | Sorted stable-partner lists exist; owners are distinct; exact support cardinality is bounded by a gap, including either sentinel. |
| [General/FiniteRevelation.lean](SmpMax/General/FiniteRevelation.lean) | Jensen's inequality on full fibers and the finite counting inequality for any separating coordinate list. |
| [General/MatchingRevelation.lean](SmpMax/General/MatchingRevelation.lean) | Identification of full fibers with matching compatibility, and the fixed-order count inequality for stable matchings. |
| [General/RevelationGap.lean](SmpMax/General/RevelationGap.lean) | Nearest revealed cuts, the clear-window equivalence, and the actual permutation support bound. |
| [General/PermutationCounting.lean](SmpMax/General/PermutationCounting.lean) | Exact first-position and first-two-position counts by transposition bijections. |
| [General/WindowEvents.lean](SmpMax/General/WindowEvents.lean) | Long gaps covered by a first clear window and later windows with revealed predecessors. |
| [General/FiniteProbability.lean](SmpMax/General/FiniteProbability.lean) | Uniform finite averages, normalized cardinalities, and union bounds. |
| [General/GapTail.lean](SmpMax/General/GapTail.lean) | Pr(K>=k)<=2/(k+1), uniformly in list length, pivot, and fixed injective owners. |
| [General/LogTail.lean](SmpMax/General/LogTail.lean) | Exact finite logarithmic tail-sum identity and expected-gap estimate. |
| [General/LogCutoff.lean](SmpMax/General/LogCutoff.lean) | A telescoping tail proves E(log K)<=B_N at every positive cutoff. |
| [General/PermutationRevelation.lean](SmpMax/General/PermutationRevelation.lean) | Actual permutation costs and their average prove count<=exp(n*B_N). |
| [General/LogEnclosure.lean](SmpMax/General/LogEnclosure.lean) | Analytic logarithm enclosures derived from proved series bounds. |
| [General/LogCertificate.lean](SmpMax/General/LogCertificate.lean) | Generated proposed rational bounds, individually proved by `norm_num`, establish B_512<log(833/250). |
| [General/EntropyUpperBound.lean](SmpMax/General/EntropyUpperBound.lean) | The final strict bound count<(833/250)^n for every positive n and every profile. |
| [General/RefinedLogBound.lean](SmpMax/General/RefinedLogBound.lean) | Sharper telescoping remainder 1/(2N)+3/(2(N+1)), uniform in every partner-list length. |
| [General/RefinedLogCertificate.lean](SmpMax/General/RefinedLogCertificate.lean) | Ten-term logarithm enclosures and 511 prefix bounds certify the refined 3.331974 target. |
| [General/RefinedEntropyUpperBound.lean](SmpMax/General/RefinedEntropyUpperBound.lean) | Abstract averaged-support assembly and the strict bound count<(1665987/500000)^n for every positive n and every profile. |
| [General/SuccessorPropagation.lean](SmpMax/General/SuccessorPropagation.lean) | Crossing a worse stable partner worsens its old owner; this propagates to the next owner and gives additional support exclusions. |
| [General/SuccessorCharging.lean](SmpMax/General/SuccessorCharging.lean) | Each exception charges a non-two-cycle with multiplicity at most two; local weighted savings imply a global saving. |
| [General/ShortSideSaving.lean](SmpMax/General/ShortSideSaving.lean) | At most one worse partner improves the gap tails at three and four, giving a fixed uniform entropy saving. |
| [General/StructuralLogCertificate.lean](SmpMax/General/StructuralLogCertificate.lean) | Exact saving comparisons and B_512-log(3)/60<log(3.272); no full 3.272 counting theorem is asserted. |
| [General/BidirectionalPropagation.lean](SmpMax/General/BidirectionalPropagation.lean) | Crossing a better stable partner improves her old owner; propagation to the next owner gives a lower barrier. |
| [General/BidirectionalGapSaving.lean](SmpMax/General/BidirectionalGapSaving.lean) | A product identity permits the two directional losses on a common gap to be added; support and threshold consequences. |
| [General/BidirectionalLogCertificate.lean](SmpMax/General/BidirectionalLogCertificate.lean) | Strengthened local-saving and coincidence comparisons, and B_512-2*delta<log(3.2); the final counting theorem is assembled below. |
| [General/RelativeOrderProbability.lean](SmpMax/General/RelativeOrderProbability.lean) | Exact counts for three ordered first labels and for one or two labels before a pivot, with all remaining designated labels after it. |
| [General/ExtendedRevelation.lean](SmpMax/General/ExtendedRevelation.lean) | Entropy counting for every injective rank assignment and for an arbitrary finite sampling space; auxiliary labels add no matching coordinates. |
| [General/FiniteAverageAlgebra.lean](SmpMax/General/FiniteAverageAlgebra.lean) | Linearity and event-contribution bounds, including overlap justified pointwise. |
| [General/LocalGapEvents.lean](SmpMax/General/LocalGapEvents.lean) | Exact local event probabilities and a formula covering all propagation-witness coincidences. |
| [General/LocalDirectionalSaving.lean](SmpMax/General/LocalDirectionalSaving.lean) | Expected short-side, first-step, and second-step directional savings, including every coincidence case. |
| [General/GapSides.lean](SmpMax/General/GapSides.lean) | The common gap equals one plus its two side lengths; clear runs and revealed boundaries determine those lengths. |
| [General/LocalGapGeometry.lean](SmpMax/General/LocalGapGeometry.lean) | Both orientations instantiate the local event geometry in the same padded gap. |

## Exporters

Three executables, declared in `lakefile.toml`, print DIMACS and cube
ids from the definitions above. They are the only bridge between the
theorem statements and the files the solvers and cake_lpr saw; the
printed output is what the identity checks compare against.

| executable | source | command |
|---|---|---|
| `export_cnf` | `ExportFiveCnf.lean` (order 5) | `lake build export_cnf`, then run `.lake/build/bin/export_cnf` in an empty directory: writes `perms120.txt`, the 120 production cubes `cubeL000.cnf` … `cubeL119.cnf` (`cubeCNF row`, 17 slots) and the 120 positive controls `cubeL16_000.cnf` … `cubeL16_119.cnf` (`cubeCNF16 row`, 16 slots). |
| `export_sched_cnf` | `ExportSixCnf.lean` (order 6) | `export_sched_cnf OUT [--n=N] [--k=K] [--prefix=a,b;c,d,e] [--stop]`: the base formula `schedCNFn N K` (defaults N = 6, K = 49, i.e. `schedCNF49`), or the cube formula for a prefix in the driver's id syntax; `--stop` closes the cube. Examples: open cube `0,1;2,3` is `--prefix='0,1;2,3'`; closed cube `0,1;stop` is `--prefix='0,1' --stop`; the root cube `stop` is `--stop` alone. Quote the argument (the ids contain semicolons). |
| `export_cubes6` | `ExportSixCubes.lean` (order 6) | `export_cubes6 OUT` prints the ids of `canonicalCubes2` (the root cubes); `--parents=FILE` prints `parent<TAB>child` for every `extendCanon` child of each id in FILE; `--final` prints the ids of `finalCubes` (the certified leaves); `--units=FILE` prints each id's unit clauses (`prefixUnits` then `stopUnits`, DIMACS lines joined by `\|`), the input of `tools/campaign/verify_lean_hashes.py`. |

Build all three with `lake build export_cnf export_sched_cnf export_cubes6`;
binaries land in `.lake/build/bin/`. The full identity-check recipe
(what to compare with the journal, expected line counts and hashes) is in
`docs/verification.md`; the recorded run is `results/f6/campaign-2026-09-08/lean_identity.txt`.

## Build, axiom and kernel-replay commands

From this directory (`lean`):

```bash
lake exe cache get          # prebuilt Mathlib
lake build                  # kernel-checks every theorem
! grep -rn sorry SmpMax/     # must print nothing

printf 'import SmpMax.Five.ExactMaximum\n#print axioms f5_eq_16_of_unsat\n' > /tmp/ax5.lean
lake env lean /tmp/ax5.lean
# 'f5_eq_16_of_unsat' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]

lake env lean /tmp/ax6.lean
```

every module re-checked by the kernel; silent exit 0 per module, about
8 s each; the recorded run of 2026-09-09 is
`results/f6/campaign-2026-09-08/leanchecker_2026-09-09.txt`, 38 / 38 clean before this path migration):

```bash
for m in $(grep -oE '^import SmpMax\.[[:alnum:]_.]+' SmpMax.lean | sed 's/import //') SmpMax; do
  lake env leanchecker "$m" || exit 1
done
```
